claims.title: Hijacked contributor account swaps OVHcloud CLI GitHub release archives for info-stealers
claims.summary: On October 19, 2026, an attacker used a compromised contributor's GitHub account to replace download archives (and checksums) on five OVHcloud CLI releases (v0.11.0–v0.15.0) with secret-stealing binaries, live for up to 94 minutes. Release immutability was not enabled; OVHcloud removed the files and published a clean immutable v0.16.0.

claims.title: Gheist campaign abuses stolen GitHub tokens to dump repository secrets
claims.summary: Wiz Research reported a campaign, tracked since September 15, 2026, that uses stolen GitHub tokens to plant 'sync-check' workflows that print base32-encoded secrets to run logs (evading masking), then delete the runs; over 13,500 branches across 850+ accounts. GitHub's approval hold blocked public-repo runs, but exploitation succeeded in private repos and GitHub Enterprise Server.

claims.title: 'testmetest' npm worm weaponizes 42 GitHub repositories to steal credentials
claims.summary: JFrog researchers found 42 compromised GitHub repositories from 11 legitimate owners used in a worm-style npm campaign that harvests tokens, abuses GitHub OIDC to obtain npm publishing credentials, and plants fake CodeQL workflows and IDE/AI-tool execution hooks. The malware includes a wiper triggered by token revocation.

claims.title: Hidden commands in GitHub issues target 61 public repos in supply-chain campaign
claims.summary: Radware found 83 malicious GitHub issues, PRs and comments from 74 likely-compromised accounts, posted largely within 43 minutes on September 1, hiding shell commands in HTML comments that vulnerable workflows executed to exfiltrate environment variables. Execution was confirmed in two cases; repos hit included Trivy, Brave and MLflow.

claims.title: Apple backports fix for exploited CoreGraphics zero-day CVE-2026-86950 to iOS 18.7.11
claims.summary: On October 26, 2026, Apple released iOS/iPadOS 18.7.11 for older devices (iPhone XS/XR, etc.) fixing CVE-2026-86950, a CoreGraphics out-of-bounds write that Apple says may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals. It was first patched in iOS 26.7.1 in late September.
